rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account makes the youths sons of nobles under the pagan king Daqyus, Romans who followed Jesus; another places them before Jesus.
rows.anchor: قوم من أبناء أشراف مدينة دقيوس الملك الكافر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Daqyanus, after Jesus, imposed idol worship in Ephesus or Tarsus; seven young secret worshippers fled with a shepherd and dog, and God blinded pursuers before they sealed the cave.
rows.anchor: إن ملكا من الملوك يقال له دقيانوس ظهر على مدينة من مدائن الروم

rows.speaker: مجاهد عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: In another account, the youths learned faith from a disciple or earlier believers, rejected the king's idols, and answered his summons with words resembling 18:14–16.
rows.anchor: وروى مجاهد عن ابن عباس أيضا أن هؤلاء الفتية كانوا في دين ملك يعبد الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported version says the king called them immature, delayed punishment, and sent them home to reconsider before a deadline; they resolved to flee while he was away.
rows.anchor: إنكم شبان أغمار لا عقول لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One escape account has them playing polo and a ball toward their route to hide their departure; another says imprisoned youths slipped away while playing at a public feast.
rows.anchor: خرجوا فيما روي يلعبون بالصولجان

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: A disciple of Jesus worked in a bathhouse, converted local youths, then fled with them after the king's son and a prostitute died there and the group was blamed.
rows.anchor: أن أول أمرهم إنما كان حواري لعيسى بن مريم جاء إلى مدينة أصحاب الكهف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The dog was either their hunting dog or a shepherd's dog that followed the shepherd and youths; it was called Himran or Qitmir.
rows.anchor: وروي أنهم وجدوا في طريقهم راعيا له كلب فاتبعهم الراعي على رأيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths' foreign names have weak transmission; al-Tabari lists Maksalmina as eldest spokesman and Yemlikha as the one sent with money, among six others.
rows.anchor: وأما أسماء أهل الكهف فأعجمية، والسند في معرفتها واه

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The dog belonged to Maksalmina, the eldest youth and owner of sheep.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: وكان الكلب لمكسلمينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story establishes fleeing with one's religion and leaving family, homeland, wealth, and friends to escape persecution; the Prophet and Companions did likewise.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية صريحة في الفرار بالدين وهجرة الأهل والبنين والقرابات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Retreat to mountains, caves, or solitude is a prophetic and saintly practice and is especially favored by many scholars amid fitna and corruption.
rows.anchor: فسكنى الجبال ودخول الغيران، والعزلة عن الخلق

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: Seclusion can be practiced in mountains, at coasts and frontier posts, or at home; a report advises hiding and guarding one's tongue during fitna.
rows.anchor: الاعتزال عن الناس يكون مرة في الجبال والشعاب، ومرة في السواحل

rows.speaker: طائفة من العلماء
rows.claim: A group defines seclusion as inwardly and practically separating from evil while remaining among people.
rows.anchor: اعتزال الشر وأهله بقلبك وعملك، إن كنت بين أظهرهم

rows.speaker: ابن المبارك
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mubarak defines seclusion as joining people when they remember God and remaining silent when they discuss other matters.
rows.anchor: أن تكون مع القوم فإذا خاضوا في ذكر الله فخض معهم

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: A report says the believer who mixes with people and patiently bears harm is better than one who avoids people and does not bear their harm.
rows.anchor: المؤمن الذي يخالط الناس ويصبر على أذاهم أفضل من المؤمن الذي لا يخالطهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: A saying that al-Baghawi transmits as a mursal report from al-Hasan and others calls believers' homes their cloisters.
rows.anchor: " من مراسيل الحسن وغيره

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: In response to Uqba ibn Amir asking about salvation, the Prophet advises holding the tongue, staying home, and weeping over one's sin.
rows.anchor: يا عقبة أمسك عليك لسانك وليسعك بيتك وابك على خطيئتك

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: A Bukhari report describes a time when a Muslim's best property will be sheep taken to mountain heights and rain-fed places to flee fitna for faith.
rows.anchor: يأتي على الناس زمان خير مال الرجل المسلم الغنم يتبع بها شعف الجبال

rows.speaker: الحسن بن واقد
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says that in year 180 AH celibacy, seclusion, and retreat to mountain tops become permitted for the community.
rows.anchor: إذا كانت سنة ثمانين ومائة فقد حلت لأمتي العزبة والعزلة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: A long report says that in a corrupt age only flight from peak to peak or stone to stone preserves religion; family may ruin a person by demanding unaffordable provision.
rows.anchor: لا يسلم لذي دين دينه إلا من فر بدينه من شاهق إلى شاهق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People differ in capacity: mountain-cave retreat is the highest state, home seclusion suits others, and some can mix outwardly while remaining inwardly distinct.
rows.anchor: أحوال الناس في هذا الباب تختلف، فرب رجل تكون له قوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some veterans of Badr stayed inside their homes after Uthman's killing and did not leave again except for burial.
rows.anchor: اعتزل رجال من أهل بدر فلزموا بيوتهم بعد قتل عثمان

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb counsels a would-be recluse that people need one another, advising him to hear without listening, see without looking, and speak little.
rows.anchor: أصم سميعا، أعمى بصيرا، سكوتا نطوقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Any place away from people, including mosque retreat, coastal service, or home, fits the meaning of mountain solitude; mountains are named because they are common retreats.
rows.anchor: فكل موضع يبعد عن الناس فهو داخل في معناه كما ذكرنا

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: Uqba ibn Amir reports that God admires a shepherd on a mountain crag who calls and performs prayer from fear of Him, forgives him, and admits him to Paradise.
rows.anchor: يعجب ربك من راعي غنم في رأس شظية الجبل يؤذن بالصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths fled their pursuers and turned to supplication; rahma here means forgiveness and provision, while rushd means success in right guidance.
rows.anchor: لما فروا ممن يطلبهم اشتغلوا بالدعاء ولجأوا إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets their request for right guidance as asking for a safe exit from the cave.
rows.anchor: مخرجا من الغار في سلامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes rushd to mean what is correct; similarly, the Prophet resorted to prayer when troubled.
rows.anchor: ومن هذا المعنى أنه عليه السلام كان إذا حزبه أمر فزع إلى الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression describes God putting the youths to sleep and is a notably eloquent Qur'anic phrase that challenged Arab eloquence.
rows.anchor: عبارة عن إلقاء الله تعالى النوم عليهم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains the phrase as preventing them from hearing, since a sleeping person wakes when he hears.
rows.anchor: أي منعناهم عن أن يسمعوا لأن النائم إذا سمع انتبه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says their ears were blocked against incoming sounds by sleep.
rows.anchor: ضربنا على آذانهم بالنوم أي سددنا آذانهم عن نفوذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation says God answered their prayer, diverted their people's harm, and made them sleep; the readings converge in meaning.
rows.anchor: أي فاستجبنا دعاءهم، وصرفنا عنهم شر قومهم

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub compares the idiom to striking a subject's hand to stop wrongdoing or a slave's hand to stop his trading activity.
rows.anchor: هذا كقول العرب ضرب الأمير على يد الرعية إذا منعهم الفساد

rows.speaker: الأسود بن يعفر
rows.claim: Al-Aswad's verse uses the phrase 'struck the earth over me' to witness this idiom; he was blind.
rows.anchor: ضربت علي الأرض الأسداس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ears are singled out because sound most often disrupts sleep, and sleep deepens when hearing is inactive; a hadith describes Satan urinating in the ear of a long sleeper.
rows.anchor: لأنها الجارحة التي منها عظم فساد النوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adadan modifies years as counted; counting conveys a long duration since a small number needs no enumeration. It can also be an accusative of verbal noun, per Abu Ubayda.
rows.anchor: نعت للسنين أي معدودة، والقصد به العبارة عن التكثير

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda parses adadan as an accusative cognate object.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: «عددا» نصب على المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take the following statement of 300 years plus nine as specifying the duration mentioned here.
rows.anchor: بين الله تعالى عدد تلك السنين من بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths were raised from sleep; one awakened or revived is called mabʿuth because sleep prevents movement and action.
rows.anchor: ويقال لمن أحيي أو أقيم من نومه مبعوث لأنه كان ممنوعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Linaʿlama means bringing God's already-known fact into existence and observation, not acquiring new knowledge; God already knew which party counted the duration better.
rows.anchor: عبارة عن خروج ذلك الشيء إلى الوجود ومشاهدته

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri reads the verb in the passive-person form liyʿlama, with yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الزهري «ليعلم» بالياء

rows.speaker: الجمهور من المفسرين
rows.claim: The apparent two parties are the youths, who thought they had slept briefly, and the townspeople alive when they awoke, who had records of their story.
rows.anchor: والظاهر من الآية أن الحزب الواحد هم الفتية إذ ظنوا لبثهم قليلا

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: One group identifies the parties as two groups of unbelievers disputing how long the sleepers remained.
rows.anchor: هما حزبان من الكافرين، اختلفا في مدة أصحاب الكهف

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group identifies the parties as two groups of believers; other proposals lack connection to the verse's wording.
rows.anchor: هما حزبان من المؤمنين. وقيل غير ذلك مما لا يرتبط بألفاظ الآية

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali parses amadan as a direct object.
rows.anchor: نصب على المفعول به قاله أبو علي

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ parses amadan as a specification accusative.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: نصب على التمييز

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses amadan as an adverb of time, the endpoint of their stay.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: نصب على الظرف، أي أي الحزبين أحصى للبثهم في الأمد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses amadan as a number, an approximate interpretation by meaning.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: «أمدا» معناه عددا، وهذا تفسير بالمعنى

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari makes amadan governed by the verb labithu; Ibn Atiyya rejects this analysis, while noting a possible analogy from rare quadriliteral forms.
rows.anchor: وقال الطبري: «أمدا» منصوب ب«لبثوا»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A dangling citation describes the Prophet's basin water as whiter than milk and quotes Umar saying it is more neglected than its counterpart.
rows.anchor: وقال في صفة حوضه صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ماؤه أبيض من اللبن»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After noting disagreement about the youths' duration, God states that He recounts their true story and knows its actual course.
rows.anchor: اختلافا وقع في أمد الفتية، عقب بالخبر عن أنه

rows.speaker: أهل اللسان
rows.claim: The youths are called young men, and linguistic authorities say faith is the foundation of futuwwa.
rows.anchor: حكم لهم بالفتوة حين آمنوا بلا واسطة كذلك قال أهل اللسان

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Al-Junayd defines futuwwa as giving generously, refraining from harm, and not complaining.
rows.anchor: الفتوة بذل الندى وكف الأذى وترك الشكوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another definition is avoiding forbidden things and hastening to virtuous acts; al-Qurtubi prefers it as encompassing the other definitions.
rows.anchor: الفتوة اجتناب المحارم واستعجال المكارم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their increased guidance means God made righteous action easy for them, including devoting themselves to God, avoiding people, and renouncing worldly life; this adds to faith.
rows.anchor: يسرناهم للعمل الصالح من الانقطاع إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says God increased their guidance through the shepherd's dog: after they chased it, it prayed, spoke of knowing God forty years before them, and they were guided further.
rows.anchor: فوالله لقد عرفت الله قبل أن تعرفوه بأربعين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tying their hearts means God gave them firm resolve and patience to confess God's sole lordship before unbelievers; fear resembles loosening, while courage resembles binding.
rows.anchor: عبارة عن شدة عزم وقوة صبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image also appears in the account of Moses' mother and in 8:11, where God binds hearts and steadies feet.
rows.anchor: ومنه الربط على قلب أم موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths' standing may describe their confrontation before the pagan king, where rejecting his religion required strength against his power.
rows.anchor: أن يكون هذا وصف مقامهم بين يدي الملك الكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says noble youths gathered outside town without appointment; their eldest voiced a conviction about God and the others affirmed it together.
rows.anchor: فخرجوا واجتمعوا وراء تلك المدينة من غير ميعاد فقال أسنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation takes standing as their decisive resolve to flee to God and oppose their people.
rows.anchor: أن يعبر بالقيام عن انبعاثهم بالعزم إلى الهروب إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shatatan means a grossly unjust or impossible statement: invoking another deity would be a wrong and falsehood.
rows.anchor: أي لئن دعونا إلها غيره فقد قلنا إذا جورا ومحالا

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says Sufis rely on the youths' standing and speaking as a basis for devotional practice.
rows.anchor: تعلقت الصوفية في القيام والقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi rejects that inference: the youths praised God, thanked Him, then fled in fear, which has no relation to foot-stamping or dancing to attractive voices.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء قاموا فذكروا الله على هدايته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says such dancing is forbidden according to a group of scholars and points to his discussion of 17:37.
rows.anchor: ثم هذا حرام عند جماعة العلماء

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الطرسوسي
rows.claim: Asked about Sufi practice, al-Tarsusi says dancing and ecstatic display began with the Samiri's people, who danced around the calf; he calls it pagan worship.
rows.anchor: وأما الرقص والتواجد فأول من أحدثه أصحاب السامري لما اتخذ لهم عجلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words may be God's instruction to the youths or, in Ibn Atiyya's account, a speech by their leader Yemlikha.
rows.anchor: هو من قول الله لهم

rows.speaker: الغزنوي
rows.claim: Al-Ghaznawi instead names Maksalmina as their leader who urged retreat to the cave.
rows.anchor: قال لهم ذلك أي إذ اعتزلتموهم واعتزلتم ما يعبدون

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: If the townspeople knew only idols and did not know God, illa Allah is a disjoint exception from what they worshipped.
rows.anchor: وهذا على تقدير إن الذين فر أهل الكهف منهم لا يعرفون الله

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: If the townspeople knew God but associated idols with Him, the exception is connected because the youths left every object of worship except God.
rows.anchor: وإن فرضنا أنهم يعرفون الله كما كانت العرب تفعل لكنهم يشركون أصنامهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The reading in Ibn Masud's codex, 'what they worship besides God,' is Qatada's explanatory gloss.
rows.anchor: وفي مصحف عبد الله بن مسعود «وما يعبدون من دون الله». قال قتادة هذا تفسيرها

rows.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
rows.claim: Al-Khurasani says the youths came from a people worshipping God alongside idols, and they abandoned idol worship while keeping worship of God.
rows.anchor: كان فتية من قوم يعبدون الله ويعبدون معه آلهة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: On Qatada's reading, illa means 'other than' and ma is accusative, coordinated with the pronoun in 'you left them.'
rows.anchor: فعلى ما قال قتادة تكون «إلا» بمنزلة غير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths decide that after separating from unbelievers and their worship they will make the cave their refuge, trust God's mercy, and ask for a worldly convenience while secure about the afterlife.
rows.anchor: فلنجعل الكهف مأوى ونتكل على الله فإنه سيبسط لنا رحمته

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر محمد بن علي بن الحسين
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar says the People of the Cave were polishers and names the cave Hayyum.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو جعفر محمد بن علي بن الحسين رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mirfaq is read with mīm kasra or fatḥa and denotes something used for comfort; usage also distinguishes the arm joint from a place or matter of assistance.
rows.anchor: قرىء بكسر الميم وفتحها، وهو ما يرتفق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun turns away from the cave at sunrise; the address is hypothetical, meaning that a viewer would see this, not that the Prophet actually saw them.
rows.anchor: إنك لو رأيتهم لرأيتهم كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazawaru means to withdraw or incline, from azwar, a slant; azwar can describe a gaze turned aside and is extended beyond eyes.
rows.anchor: و «تزاور» تتنحى وتميل من الازورار

rows.speaker: ابن أبي ربيعة
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Rabiʿa's line uses azwar for a person turning aside in fear of others.
rows.anchor: وجنبي خيفة القوم أزور

rows.speaker: عنترة
rows.claim: Antara's line uses azwara for turning aside from the impact of a spear.
rows.anchor: فازور من وقع القنا بلبانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mu'ta report describes Abd Allah ibn Rawaha's bier as slanted away from the biers of Jaʿfar and Zayd.
rows.anchor: رأى في سرير عبد الله بن رواحة ازورارا عن سرير جعفر وزيد بن حارثة

rows.speaker: أهل الحرمين وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: They assimilate the tāʾ into zāy in tazāwaru, whose underlying form is tatazāwaru.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الحرمين وأبو عمرو «تزاور» بإدغام التاء

rows.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They read tazāwaru with a light zāy.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي «تزاور» مخففة الزاي

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn Amir reads tazawwaru, like taḥmaru.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر «تزور» مثل تحمر

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ also records tazwāru, like taḥmāru; all these forms mean the same thing.
rows.anchor: وحكى الفراء «تزوار» مثل تحمار كلها بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The majority reading has the sun leave them at sunset; Mujahid glosses taqriḍuhum as 'leave them.'
rows.anchor: قرأ الجمهور بالتاء على معنى تتركهم قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses the verb as 'abandon them'; Basran authorities confirm that qarada can mean leave.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: تدعهم. النحاس: وهذا معروف في اللغة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the sun never touched them, as an honor: it passed to the cave's right at sunrise and left by its left at sunset.
rows.anchor: وهو قول ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cave faced Banat Naʿsh in Roman territory; its orientation or southern and western barriers kept sun from burning them, changing their color, or wearing their clothes.
rows.anchor: وكان كهفهم مستقبل بنات نعش في أرض الروم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the sun's course was a divine sign, not an effect of the cave opening's orientation.
rows.anchor: وذهب الزجاج إلى أن فعل الشمس كان آية من الله

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: A group reads the verb with yāʾ from qard, meaning the cave's shade cuts them off from sunlight.
rows.anchor: وقرأت فرقة «يقرضهم» بالياء من القرض وهو القطع

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another interpretation says the sun gives them only a little of its rays, perhaps beneficial in the evening.
rows.anchor: أي يصيبهم يسير منها، مأخوذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The point is that God sheltered them in a cave that protected their bodies and appearance from injury, heat, and cold; cloud or another cause could have diverted the sun.
rows.anchor: والمقصود بيان حفظهم عن تطرق البلاء وتغير الأبدان والألوان إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fajwa means a spacious part of the cave; the word has plural forms and denotes enough room for moving air to reach them.
rows.anchor: والفجوة المتسع، وجمعها فجوات وفجاء

rows.speaker: شاعر
rows.claim: The author introduces a poetic example after listing the plural forms of fajwa.
rows.anchor: وجمعها فجوات وفجاء مثل ركوة وركاء وركوات. وقال الشاعر:

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: They seemed awake because their eyes were open; another view says their frequent turning made them look awake.
rows.anchor: كانت أعينهم مفتوحة وهم نائمون فكذلك كان الرائي يحسبهم أيقاظا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ruqud is a collective description by a verbal noun, like saying a people are bowing, prostrating, or sitting.
rows.anchor: كقولهم: وهم قوم ركوع وسجود وقعود فوصف الجمع بالمصدر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God turned them from side to side so the earth would not consume their flesh.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لئلا تأكل الأرض لحومهم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra says they were turned twice each year; another report says once a year.
rows.anchor: قال أبو هريرة: كان لهم في كل عام تقليبتان

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says they were turned once every seven years.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: في كل سبع سنين مرة

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: One group says they were turned only during the final nine years, not throughout the first three hundred.
rows.anchor: إنما قلبوا في التسع الأواخر، وأما في الثلثمائة فلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators generally attribute the turning to God, but it could have been performed by an angel at God's command.
rows.anchor: ظاهر كلام المفسرين أن التقليب كان من فعل الله

rows.speaker: عمرو بن دينار
rows.claim: A saying attributed to Amr ibn Dinar claims a scorpion does not harm someone who blesses Noah, and a dog will not harm someone reciting the cave-dog clause.
rows.anchor: وإن مما أخذ على الكلب ألا يضر من حمل عليه

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Most commentators take the dog as a literal dog kept for hunting, crops, or sheep; its color traditions conflict, listing nearly every possible color.
rows.anchor: أكثر المفسرين على أنه كلب حقيقة، وكان لصيد أحدهم أو لزرعه أو غنمه

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali names the dog Rayyan; Ibn Abbas calls it Qitmir, al-Awzaʿi Mushir, Ibn Salam Basit, Kaʿb Suhya, Wahb Naqiya, and another report Qutayfur.
rows.anchor: فعن علي: ريان. ابن عباس: قطمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Keeping a dog was permitted in their time, as hunting, herding, and crop dogs are permitted under Islamic law.
rows.anchor: وكان اقتناء الكلب جائزا في وقتهم، كما هو عندنا اليوم جائز في شرعنا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says seven youths fled by night and joined a shepherd who had a dog; the shepherd adopted their faith.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هربوا ليلا، وكانوا سبعة فمروا براع معه كلب

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb says the dog returned after being chased away, raised its paws in prayer, spoke of loving God's beloved, and promised to guard them.
rows.anchor: أنا أحب أحباء الله تعالى فناموا حتى أحرسكم

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: The sound report from Ibn Umar says keeping a dog outside hunting or herding reduces one's reward by two qirats daily.
rows.anchor: من اقتنى كلبا إلا كلب صيد أو ماشية نقص من أجره كل يوم قيراطان

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: A sound report from Abu Hurayra includes crop dogs among the exceptions and states a one-qirat daily loss otherwise.
rows.anchor: من اتخذ كلبا إلا كلب ماشية أو صيد أو زرع انتقص من أجره كل يوم قيراط

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: When told Abu Hurayra's version, Ibn Umar was excused by al-Zuhri as a farmer who kept a crop dog.
rows.anchor: فقد دلت السنة الثابتة على اقتناء الكلب للصيد والزرع والماشية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Proposed reasons for the reward loss include frightening Muslims, disturbance by barking, angels' exclusion, impurity according to al-Shafiʿi, or keeping an animal without benefit.
rows.anchor: إما لترويع الكلب المسلمين وتشويشه عليهم بنباحه، أو لمنع دخول الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one- and two-qirat versions may distinguish more harmful dogs, such as the black dog called a devil, or vary by location; permitted working dogs incur no loss.
rows.anchor: وذلك يحتمل أن يكون في نوعين من الكلاب أحدهما أشد أذى من الآخر

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: A Jabir report calls a black dog with two spots a devil, in the context of the command to kill black dogs.
rows.anchor: عليكم بالأسود البهيم ذي النقطتين فإنه شيطان

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik permits a sheep dog that accompanies the flock and a crop dog that guards crops from wild animals, but not one used to guard a home from thieves.
rows.anchor: كلب الماشية المباح اتخاذه عند مالك هو الذي يسرح معها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other jurists also permit dogs guarding livestock or crops against thieves.
rows.anchor: وقد أجاز غير مالك اتخاذها لسراق الماشية والزرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dog's companionship consoles imperfect believers who love the Prophet, his family, and the righteous: if a dog is remembered with its beloved group, believers may hope for mercy.
rows.anchor: كلب أحب قوما فذكره الله معهم

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: When a man said he had little prayer, fasting, or charity but loved God and the Messenger, the Prophet told him he would be with those he loved.
rows.anchor: ما أعددت لها كثير صلاة ولا صيام ولا صدقة، ولكني أحب الله ورسوله

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas says no joy after Islam surpassed hearing that he would be with those he loved; he loved God, the Prophet, Abu Bakr, and Umar and hoped to join them.
rows.anchor: فأنا أحب الله ورسوله وأبا بكر وعمر، فأرجو أن أكون معهم

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: A group says the 'dog' was a human lookout stationed by the cave, named by analogy to a companion star of Gemini or Orion.
rows.anchor: كان قد قعد عند باب الغار طليعة لهم

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the human-guard reading is weakened by the description of outstretched forelegs, an ordinary canine posture.
rows.anchor: هذا القول يضعفه ذكر بسط الذراعين فإنها في العرف من صفة الكلب حقيقة

rows.speaker: أبو عمر المطرز
rows.claim: Abu Umar al-Mutarriz records a reading kalibihim that could mean their human keeper or their dog.
rows.anchor: أنه قرىء «وكالبهم باسط ذراعيه بالوصيد»

rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد الصادق
rows.claim: Jaʿfar al-Sadiq reads the phrase as their keeper, kalibihim.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جعفر بن محمد الصادق «وكالبهم» يعني صاحب الكلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basit is an active participle used with past reference because the verse narrates a scene rather than reporting the dog's action as a new event; a forearm runs from elbow to middle finger.
rows.anchor: أعمل اسم الفاعل وهو بمعنى المضي لأنها حكاية حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dog may have stretched its forelegs because of the long duration, or it may have been asleep, perhaps with open eyes as a sign.
rows.anchor: ثم قيل: بسط ذراعيه لطول المدة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Ibn Jubayr gloss al-wasid as the cave courtyard; Ibn Abbas also says it means the door, and Ata says the threshold.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد وابن جبير، أي فناء الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poem uses waṣīd for an entryway; the word can also mean a closed door or closely growing plants.
rows.anchor: بأرض فضاء لا يسد وصيدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anyone who looked toward them would flee from divinely imposed terror; some attribute the reaction to the cave's eerie location or a barrier of fear around them.
rows.anchor: لما حفهم الله تعالى من الرعب واكتنفهم من الهيبة

rows.speaker: المهدوي والنحاس والزجاج والقشيري
rows.claim: They suggest that the youths' long hair and nails caused the terror; al-Qurtubi calls this unlikely because they thought they had slept only a day.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الفرار منهم لطول شعورهم وأظفارهم وذكره المهدوي

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says God preserved their sleeping appearance and clothing as a sign; only the landscape and buildings changed, so hair and nails were not altered.
rows.anchor: والصحيح في أمرهم أن الله عز وجل حفظ لهم الحالة التي ناموا عليها

rows.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وابن عباس وأهل مكة والمدينة
rows.claim: They read lammuliʾta with a doubled lām for emphatic intensification; the other readers use the lighter, more common form.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن كثير وابن عباس وأهل مكة والمدينة «لملئت منهم»

rows.speaker: المخبل السعدي
rows.claim: Al-Mukhabbal al-Saʿdi's line supplies a poetic example of the doubled form.
rows.anchor: فملىء من كعب بن عوف سلاسله

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads ruʿban with ḍamma on ʿayn; Abu Hatim says both vowelings are Arabic dialects.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حاتم: هما لغتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fararan is a circumstantial accusative; ruʿban is either a second object or a specification accusative.
rows.anchor: و«فرارا» نصب على الحال و«رعبا» مفعول ثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʿath means movement from stillness; here God awakened the youths in the same clothes and condition as before sleep.
rows.anchor: البعث: التحريك عن سكون

rows.speaker: شاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses baʿath for waking young men at dawn.
rows.anchor: وفتيان صدق قد بعثت بسحرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in li-yatasaʾalu is a consequence lām, not a purpose: their awakening resulted in their questioning, as in 28:8.
rows.anchor: واللام في قوله «ليتساءلوا» لام الصيرورة وهي لام العاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They entered the cave in the morning and awoke late in the day; their leader, called Tamlikha or Maksalmina, said God knew the duration.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنهم دخلوه غدوة وبعثهم الله في آخر النهار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas compares their silver currency to the hooves of a young camel.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كانت ورقهم كأخفاف الربع

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: These readers pronounce the rāʾ in waraqikum with kasra; other readers make it still, and both are dialects.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم «بورقكم» بكسر الراء

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة وأبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: They read waraqikum with a still rāʾ, removing the kasra as heavy; al-Zajjaj records a form with kasra on wāw.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وحمزة وأبو بكر عن عاصم «بورقكم» بسكون الراء

rows.speaker: الغزنوي
rows.claim: The youths awoke hungry, and al-Ghaznawi identifies the dispatched youth Tamlikha as the youngest.
rows.anchor: ويروى أنهم انتبهوا جياعا، وأن المبعوث هو تمليخا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city was Ephesus, also called Tarsus; its earlier name was Ephesus and it was renamed Tarsus after Islam. Ibn Abbas says their coins bore the current king's image.
rows.anchor: والمدينة: أفسوس ويقال هي طرسوس، وكان اسمها في الجاهلية أفسوس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says their silver coins carried the image of the king of their time.
rows.anchor: كان معهم دراهم عليها صورة الملك الذي كان في زمانهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Azka food means meat slaughtered lawfully because townspeople sacrificed in the name of idols; Ibn Abbas also says most inhabitants were Magians.
rows.anchor: أحل ذبيحة لأن أهل بلدهم كانوا يذبحون على اسم الصنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings of azka are more blessed, tastier, or cheaper; they may have asked for enough food for several people, with rice, raisins, or dates proposed.
rows.anchor: وقيل: «أزكى طعاما» أي أكثر بركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rizqan means food; let the delegate act discreetly in town and tell nobody, lest discovery expose the rest of the youths.
rows.anchor: أي في دخول المدينة وشراء الطعام

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says yarjumukum means stoning, the worst killing; a second view takes it as verbal abuse, but stoning is preferred because the king intended to kill them.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: معناه بالحجارة، وهو أخبث القتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account supports the validity of agency, or appointing another person to act on one's behalf.
rows.anchor: في هذه البعثة بالورق دليل على الوكالة وصحتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Examples of agency include Ali appointing Aqil before Uthman and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf and Umayya ibn Khalaf agreeing to protect each other's households.
rows.anchor: وقد وكل علي بن أبي طالب أخاه عقيلا عند عثمان

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن عوف
rows.claim: A Bukhari report says Abd al-Rahman contracted with Umayya ibn Khalaf to protect each other's dependents in Mecca and Medina; Umayya objected to the name al-Rahman.
rows.anchor: كاتبت أمية بن خلف كتابا بأن يحفظني في صاغيتي بمكة وأحفظه

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Asmaʿi explains saghiya as a man's adherents who incline toward him, from the verb meaning to incline.
rows.anchor: صاغية الرجل الذين يميلون إليه ويأتونه وهو مأخوذ من صغا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Agency is a delegated contract allowed because people need help managing affairs and not everyone can handle every task alone.
rows.anchor: الوكالة عقد نيابة، أذن الله سبحانه فيه للحاجة إليه وقيام المصلحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurists support agency from this verse, 9:60, 12:93, and many hadiths, including the report of Urwa al-Bariqi.
rows.anchor: وقد استدل علماؤنا على صحتها بآيات من الكتاب، منها هذه الآية

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir says he was sent to Khaybar and told by the Prophet to collect fifteen wasqs from his agent, using a hand on the collarbone as proof if asked.
rows.anchor: إذا أتيت وكيلي فخذ منه خمسة عشر وسقا فإن ابتغى منك آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Agency is valid in any right that can be delegated, but not for a usurper or an unlawful act.
rows.anchor: الوكالة جائزة في كل حق تجوز النيابة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Agency in this story arose from fear of discovery; scholars agree that people with an excuse may appoint agents, while most permit healthy present people too.
rows.anchor: الوكالة إنما كانت مع التقية خوف أن يشعر بهم أحد

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وسحنون
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa and Sahnun disallow agency for a person present without an excuse; Ibn al-Arabi speculates Sahnun used this against oppressors, while al-Qurtubi permits it for virtuous people.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة وسحنون: لا تجوز

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: In Abu Hurayra's report, the Prophet repaid a camel debt with a better camel, and the creditor praised him; the Prophet said the best people pay best.
rows.anchor: إن خيركم أحسنكم قضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This sound report shows a healthy person present may appoint others: the Prophet authorized his Companions to repay for him, contrary to Abu Hanifa and Sahnun.
rows.anchor: فدل هذا الحديث مع صحته على جواز توكيل الحاضر الصحيح البدن

rows.speaker: ابن خويز منداد
rows.claim: Ibn Khuwayz says the verse supports partnership because the youths shared their money, agency because they sent a buyer, and joint eating despite unequal appetites.
rows.anchor: تضمنت هذه الآية جواز الشركة لأن الورق كان لجميعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The school allows a poor person to mix donated food with a rich person's meal and a business agent to mix provisions and eat together.
rows.anchor: وقد قالوا في المضارب يخلط طعامه بطعام غيره

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says the verse does not prove shared partnership because each youth may have given money separately; he relies instead on two hadiths.
rows.anchor: ليس في الآية دليل على ذلك لأنه يحتمل أن يكون كل واحد منهم قد أعطاه منفردا

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar cites the prohibition on taking two dates together without a companion's permission as evidence about shared food.
rows.anchor: نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الاقتران إلا أن يستأذن الرجل أخاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The army-of-khabt report is less decisive because Abu Ubayda may simply have distributed equal portions rather than having everyone share one supply.
rows.anchor: وهذا دون الأول في الظهور لأنه يحتمل أن يكون أبو عبيدة يعطيهم كفافا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permission to mix with orphans as siblings and the permission to eat together or separately support shared eating; the source cites 2:220 and labels the latter 24:16.
rows.anchor: ليس عليكم جناح أن تأكلوا جميعا أو أشتاتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aʿtharna means God revealed and brought them to light; the verb is the causative form of ʿathara, originally stumbling with the foot.
rows.anchor: تعدية عثر بالهمزة، وأصل العثار في القدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Daqyanus died, a righteous king's town disputed bodily resurrection: some said only souls return, while others held that body and soul rise together.
rows.anchor: فاختلف أهل بلده في الحشر وبعث الأجساد من القبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The puzzled king prayed in ascetic clothing on ashes; a youth's old coin exposed the cave youths, and he recognized them as a sign answering his prayer.
rows.anchor: حتى لبس المسوح وقعد على الرماد وتضرع إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king and townspeople learned from the youths that the community was Muslim; after they returned to the cave, most reports say they died a true death.
rows.anchor: وأكثر الروايات على أنهم ماتوا حين حدثهم تمليخا ميتة الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their discovery restored doubters to certainty that the promised resurrection and the Hour are real, including resurrection of bodies.
rows.anchor: ورجع من كان شك في بعث الأجساد إلى اليقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When people disputed what to do, one account has the king propose a building and those aligned with the youths choose a mosque; another has Muslims prevail over a church or guesthouse proposal.
rows.anchor: فقال الملك: ابنوا عليهم بنيانا فقال الذين هم على دين الفتية: اتخذوا عليهم مسجدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other accounts say some wanted to cover and conceal the cave, or that God hid it from public view so the king proposed a marker building.
rows.anchor: وروي أن بعض القوم ذهب إلى طمس الكهف عليهم وتركهم فيه مغيبين

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar says God obscured the youths from people, which explains the proposal to build a sign over the site.
rows.anchor: أن الله تعالى أعمى على الناس حينئذ أثرهم وحجبهم عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A dream report says one youth objected to being buried in a gold chest: they were created from earth and should return to it.
rows.anchor: فإنا من التراب خلقنا وإليه نعود، فدعنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking graves as mosques, praying at them, and building over them is forbidden by the Prophetic teaching cited next.
rows.anchor: فاتخاذ المساجد على القبور والصلاة فيها والبناء عليها، إلى غير ذلك

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas curses women who frequently visit graves and those who make mosques and lamps over them; al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan.
rows.anchor: لعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم زوارات القبور والمتخذين عليها المساجد

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: A report from Aisha says churches with images were built over righteous men's graves; the Prophet calls such builders the worst of creation, and jurists forbid mosques at prophets' and scholars' graves.
rows.anchor: إن أولئك إذا كان فيهم الرجل الصالح فمات بنوا على قبره مسجدا

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: The Prophet forbids praying toward graves or sitting on them; Qurtubi explains that using a grave as a qibla can lead to worship of its occupant.
rows.anchor: لا تصلوا إلى القبور ولا تجلسوا عليها

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: A report warns of God's severe anger against people who take prophets' and righteous people's graves as mosques, closing a path toward grave worship.
rows.anchor: اشتد غضب الله على قوم اتخذوا قبور أنبيائهم وصالحيهم مساجد

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: Aisha and Ibn Abbas report that during his final illness the Prophet cursed Jews and Christians for making prophets' graves into mosques.
rows.anchor: لعنة الله على اليهود والنصارى اتخذوا قبور أنبيائهم مساجد

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: Jabir reports prohibitions on plastering graves, sitting on them, building on them, writing on them, and walking over them; al-Tirmidhi grades a version hasan sahih.
rows.anchor: نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن تجصص القبور وأن يكتب عليها

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali says the Prophet ordered him to erase every image and level every raised grave; scholars infer that prominent mounds must be removed.
rows.anchor: ألا تدع تمثالا إلا طمسته ولا قبرا مشرفا إلا سويته

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority interpret the commanded leveling as removing excess height, while retaining a recognizable, respected grave mound; Malik describes this for the Prophet and his Companions.
rows.anchor: وذهب الجمهور إلى أن هذا الارتفاع المأمور بإزالته هو ما زاد على التسنيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Large, ornate grave structures that imitate pre-Islamic glorification should be demolished; the apparent prohibition and use of worldly adornment at the afterlife's first station make them unlawful.
rows.anchor: وأما تعلية البناء الكثير على نحو ما كانت الجاهلية تفعله تفخيما وتعظيما فذلك يهدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasnīm is a grave mound about a handspan high, named from a camel's hump, and it is sprinkled with water to prevent wind scattering it.
rows.anchor: والتسنيم في القبر: ارتفاعه قدر شبر مأخوذ من سنام البعير

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi permits coating a grave with mud; Abu Hanifa forbids plaster, mud coating, and a structure above it.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي لا بأس أن يطين القبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stones may mark a grave; a report says Fatima visited Hamza's grave weekly and marked it with a stone.
rows.anchor: ولا بأس بوضع الأحجار لتكون علامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Burial in a coffin is permissible, especially in loose soil; reports describe stone coffins for Daniel and a glass coffin for Joseph until Moses recovered him.
rows.anchor: وأما الجائزة: فالدفن في التابوت وهو جائز لا سيما في الأرض الرخوة

rows.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
rows.claim: On his deathbed, Saʿd asked for a lateral niche and upright bricks as used for the Prophet; a lahd is a side chamber in firm earth, preferred by Malik and Abu Hanifa, while al-Shafiʿi prefers a trench.
rows.anchor: اتخذوا لي لحدا وانصبوا علي اللبن نصبا كما صنع برسول الله

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi permits bricks in a lahd as a kind of stone; Abu Hanifa and his companions dislike them as building material unsuited to a grave, though another view objects because fire touched the brick.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي: لا بأس به لأنه نوع من الحجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clay bricks and reeds are recommended; a bundle of reeds was reportedly placed on the Prophet's grave.
rows.anchor: ويستحب اللبن والقصب لما روي أنه وضع على قبر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حزمة من قصب

rows.speaker: أبو بكر محمد بن الفضل
rows.claim: The Hanafi jurist permits coffins where soil is loose, even iron ones, with earth beneath the deceased and light bricks at the sides to resemble a lahd.
rows.anchor: أنه جوز اتخاذ التابوت في بلادهم لرخاوة الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi explains felt lining beneath the Prophet as suited to Medina's salty ground; Shaqran reported placing it there, and al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan sahih gharib.
rows.anchor: ومن هذا المعنى جعل القطيفة في قبر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فإن المدينة سبخة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reproached the Prophet for promising Quraysh an answer the next day about the Spirit, the youths, and Dhul-Qarnayn without saying inshaAllah; revelation paused fifteen days and unbelievers spread rumors.
rows.anchor: فاحتبس الوحي عنه خمسة عشر يوما حتى شق ذلك عليه وأرجف الكفار به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One should not state a future intention as certain without attaching it to God's will; otherwise failure to do it makes the assertion a lie. The lām in li-shayʾ means 'concerning' or 'for'.
rows.anchor: وأمر في هذه الآية ألا يقول في أمر من الأمور إني أفعل غدا كذا وكذا، إلا أن يعلق ذلك بمشيئة الله

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says this is the general practice of saying inshaAllah, not the law of conditional oaths; the omitted words mean 'unless you say, if God wills.'
rows.anchor: والآية ليست في الأيمان وإنما هي في سنة الاستثناء في غير اليمين

rows.speaker: الكسائي والفراء والأخفش
rows.claim: They interpret the ellipsis as an instruction to say 'if God wills'; the Basrans instead construe it as acting by God's will.
rows.anchor: ما اختاره ابن عطية وارتضاه هو قول الكسائي والفراء والأخفش

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: A group makes the exception attach to 'do not say'; Ibn Atiyya reports al-Tabari rejected this construction as profoundly unsound.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول حكاه الطبري ورد عليه، وهو من الفساد بحيث كان الواجب ألا يحكى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rules for exception in oaths were treated earlier in the discussion of 5:89.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم القول في الاستثناء في اليمين وحكمه في «المائدة»

rows.speaker: محمد الكوفي المفسر
rows.claim: Muhammad al-Kufi says the following prayer is a formula everyone who forgot to say inshaAllah should recite, and it expiates the omission.
rows.anchor: إنها بألفاظها مما أمر أن يقولها كل من لم يستثن

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority take 'remember your Lord when you forget' as a general commanded supplication, not a special formula.
rows.anchor: وقال الجمهور: هو دعاء مأمور به دون هذا التخصيص

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: They interpret the reminder as saying inshaAllah when one remembers after forgetting; Ibn Abbas says even remembering after a year prevents an oath from being broken.
rows.anchor: حكي عن ابن عباس أنه إن نسي الاستثناء ثم ذكر ولو بعد سنة لم يحنث

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan limits delayed inshaAllah to the same sitting; a report from Ibn Abbas allows two years, which al-Ghaznawi treats as a devotional benefit, since legally effective exception must be continuous.
rows.anchor: الحسن: ما دام في مجلس الذكر. ابن عباس: سنتين ذكره الغزنوي

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the command means to make up any prayer one forgot when one remembers it.
rows.anchor: السدي: أي كل صلاة نسيها إذا ذكرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other glosses say to remember God lest one forget, remember Him whenever forgotten, or ask Him to restore forgotten things; remembering God when one forgets oneself or other things is the deeper sense.
rows.anchor: وقيل اذكره متى ما نسيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to the Prophet but is an opening instruction rather than an oath rule; it also applies to the whole community because such forgetfulness is common.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية مخاطبة للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، وهي استفتاح كلام على الأصح

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud's codex adds wa-qalu, 'and they said,' before the statement of duration.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود «وقالوا لبثوا»

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari says Israelites disputed how long had passed since the youths were discovered; God clarifies that 300 years and nine describe their sleep, while the later period is unknown to humans.
rows.anchor: فأخبر الله تعالى نبيه أن هذه المدة في كونهم نياما

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: On this reading, the first 'they remained' refers to sleep, and the second to the time after discovery until Muhammad's era or their bodies' decay.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: فقوله على هذا «لبثوا» الأول

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says their later, unspecified stay extended until the Qur'an was revealed.
rows.anchor: مجاهد: إلى وقت نزول القرآن

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the later period extended until they died; another report says the nine's units were unclear to people, so knowledge was referred to God.
rows.anchor: الضحاك: إلى أن ماتوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent Arabic sense is nine years because years were just named; the historical appearance is that the youths entered the cave not long after Jesus while some disciples remained.
rows.anchor: وظاهر كلام العرب المفهوم منه أنها أعوام

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri says the nine cannot mean nights or hours because the preceding word years supplies the understood unit, as in a hundred dirhams and five.
rows.anchor: لا يفهم من التسع تسع ليال وتسع ساعات لسبق ذكر السنين

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali supplies an omitted noun: they remained an additional nine years.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو علي «وازدادوا تسعا» أي ازدادوا لبث

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says listeners asked whether the 300 were years, months, weeks, or days, so God specified 'years.'
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: لما نزلت { ولبثوا في كهفهم

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash explains nine as the difference between 300 solar years and their equivalent lunar years, about one year per 33⅓ solar years; al-Ghaznawi gives a similar account.
rows.anchor: لبثوا ثلثمائة سنة شمسية بحساب الأيام فلما كان الإخبار هنا للنبي العربي

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read '300' with an indefinite hundred and accusative sinin, interpreting the order as '300 years'; sinin is apposition, explication, or specification.
rows.anchor: قرأ الجمهور «ثلثمائة سنين» بتنوين مائة ونصب سنين

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisai join miʾa to sinin without tanwin, treating the plural as equivalent to singular sana.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي بإضافة مائة إلى سنين، وترك التنوين

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali notes that numbers normally joined to singular nouns can also be joined to plurals; Ibn Masud's codex instead has '300 year.'
rows.anchor: هذه الأعداد التي تضاف في المشهور إلى الآحاد نحو ثلثمائة رجل وثوب

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak reads thalathamiʾata sunun with nominative plural ending.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك «ثلثمائة سنون» بالواو

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr has a variant reading of tisʿan with fatḥa on tāʾ; the majority use kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو بخلاف «تسعا» بفتح التاء وقرأ الجمهور بكسرها

rows.speaker: الفراء والكسائي وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: They parse the construction in the order 'they remained years, three hundred.'
rows.anchor: التقدير ولبثوا في كهفهم سنين ثلثمائة
